citation: docs/mip/0010-api-for-other-tools.md, section 3; proto/muster_api.proto, its header's Ending
why: The daemon ends a connection with an Ended saying why when it can, with the epoch and the number of the last event the client was sent, so a client knows whether to connect again at once and where it had got to. Falling behind is held by a Rust test, since no conversation can stop reading for long enough. Each case is a conversation in protobuf's canonical JSON; docs/testing.md has the steps and tokens.

cases.name: a handoff ends a subscription as replaced, and the same socket serves the successor
cases.why: A newer daemon took over the panes, so the client connects to the same socket, where the successor answers as the same daemon in a new instance, and subscribes again (the header, Ending). The identity stays; the instance changes.

cases.name: a daemon stopping ends a subscription saying where it had got to
cases.why: An orderly stop ends every connection as STOPPING, with `reached`, the number of the last event written, so a client that comes back later knows what it had (the header, Ending). A group made by an agent joining it is three events, a number nothing else on the daemon adds to, so `reached` is exact.
